Malware

Malware is software designed to harm a system or misuse its access.

Ransomware
Blocks access to files or systems and demands payment. Some incidents also involve stolen data.
Trojans
Masquerade as legitimate programs or files to persuade someone to run them.
Spyware
Collects information such as activity or sensitive data without informed consent.

Threats

Some attacks exploit trust in a message, supplier or service.

Phishing
Messages or sites impersonate trusted people or services to obtain information or prompt an unsafe action.
Supply-chain attacks
A compromise at a supplier, software dependency or service provider can affect the people and systems that rely on it.

Protect Yourself

Start with the accounts you use for password resets and the devices you rely on every day.

  • Passwords and account security

    Use a different password for each account. Start with the inbox that receives your reset links.

  • Multi-factor authentication

    Add another way to verify a sign-in and keep recovery codes somewhere you can access safely.

  • Phishing awareness

    If a message asks you to sign in, open the service independently through its app or a saved address.

  • Device security and software updates

    Turn on automatic updates where available and restart when an update requires it.

  • Safe browsing and HTTPS

    Check the site’s address before signing in. HTTPS protects the connection to that address.

Online Privacy

Review which apps can access your location, camera, microphone or contacts. Check the privacy controls on shared devices and browsers, too.
